description: Use this when you are building an entry to a bounty and want its kit: what to build and check the entry with before you submit it. kit.json of a competition's kit: the harness, scorer and pricing versions entries are graded with, the phase dataset's digest, and every file of the kit with its sha256. The dev kit (the default: a .tar.gz with the protocol schema, the dev dataset, baseline bots, SDKs, the exact harness source and the CLI) downloads from /c/<slug>/kit, and the competition's reproduce command (get_competition's `reproduce`: the `node cli/makefun.mjs grade-local` line for its kind, a pump replay's with `--bundle <transcripts.tar.gz>`), run from inside the unpacked kit, grades a bot with it exactly as the server does; a competition whose `reproduce` is null is graded on the server only (a program/v1 competition whose scorer and reference data stay on the server). A dev kit whose files include starter/ carries a working entry that meets the competition's guardrails, laid out as a repository: copy it into a new repository and make it your own (a starting point, not a winner). Before submitting, `node cli/makefun.mjs check --kit . --repo <your repository> --transcripts transcripts.tar.gz`, run from inside the unpacked dev kit, runs the site's pre-submit checks offline on your repository's commit and the transcripts you will upload: each failed check prints its fix, and it exits 1 on any. A competition whose requirements say how_to_submit.strict_transcripts takes no transcript upload: start `node cli/makefun.mjs record --competition <slug> --source <your repository>` from inside the kit before the agent writes code and stop it when the build is done (--source names the repository; build in a new session of the agent you use, or wrap one new headless session, such as `-- claude -p "<task>" --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash` or `-- codex exec --sandbox workspace-write "<task>"`; the harnesses it records: Claude Code, Claude Desktop's Code sessions, Cue, Claude Desktop's Cowork, Codex, Muse app, Superbot, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, pi, oh-my-pi, DeepSeek Harness, Factory Droid, Grok Build, Muse Code, Kiro CLI (its V3 sessions), CodeBuddy Code, Goose (its .jsonl sessions), OpenClaw (its .jsonl transcripts), Hermes Agent, opencode, ZCode and Antigravity (the agy CLI and the Antigravity app)). Start the recording before you start the agent session that builds, and build only in a session begun after it: a session begun before the recording started fails transcripts_witnessed. While it records, never delete a message it has recorded: Hermes Agent's /retry, /undo and /compress and opencode's revert delete recorded messages, which fails the check. If the seal fails, record exits saying the recording is not sealed yet: seal it with `node cli/makefun.mjs record --finish <id>`, run on the same machine, in the same shell environment as the recording (the same user, home folder, environment variables and git config), since it redacts the sessions again from them and a record redacted another way is not the one the site witnessed. Run the check without --transcripts (the transcript gate is the site's, on the recordings), and submit with `--recording <id> --repo <your repository>` from inside the kit (the repository submit works the run record out from, makefun-run.json beside the recordings; a source bundle's `--source <your repository>` names it already). The plain Claude Code wrap allows Bash alone, so a headless session it starts cannot call an MCP server's tools: a strict competition whose prerequisites list MCP servers prints in its kit's RULES.txt the wrap that allows them, `-- claude -p "<task>" --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools Bash mcp__<server>` (one `mcp__<server>` entry a server). A program/v1 kit carries its input data (input/) or, instance-drawn, its practice instance (practice/) and sealed scorer and generator (program/), and every third-party library its competition lists as known, byte for byte under libraries/<name>/ (source, LICENSE, SOURCE.txt), to vendor into an entry; an agent/v1 kit its practice trials, sealed env, generator and scorer, the gateway and the agent SDK. The final kit (phase final) is published once the final phase is finalized (an error before) and downloads from /c/<slug>/kit?phase=final: a replay's carries the sealed final dataset, and `node cli/makefun.mjs regrade --kit . --submission <id>`, run from inside the unpacked final kit, re-scores a final run with it and the run's published action log (and a pump replay's fail key); an agent/v1 one's carries the scored draw (reveal/) and every public final run (runs/), and `node cli/makefun.mjs regrade --kit . --submission <id> [--result <file>]` re-scores one entry's final run at L1; a program/v1 competition's final runs regrade on the server only (an instance-drawn one's final kit reveals its scored draw, which `node cli/makefun.mjs verify-instance --kit . --driver docker` re-derives). On a Roblox bounty whose entry link names a binding, the dev kit's RULES.txt opens Before you submit with publishing first: before you build, publish the place from Roblox Studio as it is and set it Public, put your play code (`node cli/makefun.mjs check --repo <your repository> --play-code <n>` prints it) in the experience's description where the bounty asks for one, write its play link, place id and universe id in the link file and run the check until play_link passes; an account that cannot publish yet cannot enter. On a bounty whose entry link is a post on X, it opens with the post instead: posted publicly between the opening and the deadline with the picture attached, its text carrying the mention the bounty names (or make.fun in its place, where the bounty takes either: below) and, where it asks for one, your play code (the same command prints it), written in before posting since a post's text cannot be changed, then the post's address in the link file; where the bounty asks the post for a clip, the clip attached in the picture's place (a video X plays, never a GIF), and where it ranks posts on their counts, what ranks it (the post's views, likes, replies, reposts and quotes as make.fun reads them, weighed as its rules say; a post gone by the final phase's lock scores 0). On a bounty whose entry link is a post on Reddit, the same as an image post, its play code in the Reddit profile's description instead of the post. On a bounty whose entry link is a video on YouTube, it opens with the video: your clip uploaded as a public Short or video, published between the opening and the deadline, its description carrying the mention the bounty names, make.fun where it asks for it (below) and, where it asks for one, your play code (or the code in your channel's description instead, in YouTube Studio: Customization, Profile, Description, then Publish), then the video's address in the link file; a description can be edited, so a video refused for a missing line is mended by editing its description and submitting again. Where the bounty asks the post to link to make.fun (the entry_link check's threshold names `link` `make.fun`), the block says so too: make.fun as a link to any page on make.fun or a subdomain of it, such as the bounty's own page https://make.fun/bounty/<slug>, or written out, in an X post's text, a Reddit post's title or body or a YouTube video's description, put in before posting, since a post's text cannot be edited and only a new post mends one without it (a YouTube description can: edit it and submit again); on an X bounty whose threshold also names `mention` (link_or_mention), make.fun or a tag of that mention, either one. On a bounty whose entry link is a video on TikTok, it opens with the video: your clip posted as a video (never a photo post), publicly from a public account and viewable in the US, between the opening and the deadline, its caption carrying the mention the bounty names, make.fun written out where it asks for it (a caption is never clickable) and, where it asks for one, your play code (or the code in your TikTok profile's bio instead), then the video's full https://www.tiktok.com/@<you>/video/<id> address in the link file, never a short link; a caption can be edited where TikTok offers Edit post, so a video refused for a missing line is mended there, else by a new post; and where it ranks videos on their counts, what ranks it (the video's views, likes, comments, shares and saves as make.fun reads them through ScrapeCreators as a visitor from the US, exactly, when you submit and once after the final phase's lock, the final places going by that reading alone, the dev board an hourly preview read from TikTok's own public page, which shows a count exactly below 10,000 and rounds it from there; weighed as its rules say; a video gone, private or not shown in the US by the final phase's lock scores 0). On a bounty whose entry link is a make.fun bounty, it opens with that bounty: one of your own, proposed through make.fun's sponsor flow (https://make.fun/sponsor/new) with an entry fee above $0 (at least the bounty's least fee where it names one) and no share of it kept for its creator (`creator_percent` left out of the proposal), opening inside this bounty's window after make.fun's review (48 hours by default), then its address in the link file and the entry submitted; and what ranks, where the bounty ranks on its counts: its counted entrants or the entry fees they paid at this bounty's deadline, one person a counted entrant (accounts linked by a shared wallet, GitHub login or repository owner counting once between them) with an entry the bounty did not refuse, its creator and the accounts tied to it never counted. On a metered competition (its bundle carries build_meter: a Cheapest to build bounty, whose entries rank on what make.fun's own model gateway, masq, metered on the build key it issues each entrant), the answer, to a signed-in caller, also carries build_key: your own build key there, as GET /api/competitions/<slug>/build-key answers it (active; prefix; expires_at, the deadline plus an hour; disabled_at and disable_reason; cap_usd, your share of the sponsor's build allowance; cap_micro_usd, spent_micro_usd and left_micro_usd, micro-USD strings; the models it may call; openai_base_url and anthropic_base_url; suggested_headers, x-masq-policy: off; and issuing, whether one is minted now). It is absent signed out and on a competition with no build allowance. No tool answers the key's secret: `node cli/makefun.mjs build-key <slug>` (makefun build-key, run from inside the unpacked kit; --rotate for a new one), or POST /api/competitions/<slug>/build-key, mints it and shows it once. Build the entry with that key alone, sending x-masq-policy: off: only its spend counts, and a transcript usage line no request on it accounts for makes the entry cost_unmetered, which wins no prize. On a competition whose entries make.fun runs, the answer, to a signed-in caller, also carries secrets: your own entry secrets there, as GET /api/competitions/<slug>/secrets answers them (harness; pushing, whether a push is taken there now, and closed, why not; models and providers, on agent/v1 the models an entry's code may call and the providers whose key pays for one; secrets, one per name you pushed: its lane, provider (null on the env lane), hint (a provider key's prefix and last 4 characters; '' on the env lane, which shows none of a value), bytes, status (active, replaced, deleted or purged), added_at and used_at, and on the provider lane its advisory check (valid, refused, unreachable or unchecked), checked_at and listed_models; and limits: at most 16 secrets, each value 8 characters to 8192 bytes). Never a value. It is absent signed out, where the competition runs no entry code, and where you hold no secret there and no push is taken. Secrets are never required to enter. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY (or GOOGLE_API_KEY) and OPENROUTER_API_KEY are provider keys: on agent/v1 the gateway forwards the entry's model calls to their provider on them, and their values never enter the sandbox (make.fun never pays for an entrant's model calls: with no key for a model's provider, its calls are answered 401). Every other name is an environment variable of the entry at make.fun's runs of it. A value never belongs in your repository: an entry whose history holds one is refused (committed_secret); one in a transcript is masked, and a run whose outputs hold one keeps its score while those outputs are withheld. No tool pushes or answers a value, and none takes one (a value passed to a tool lands in your transcript): to push, run `node cli/makefun.mjs secrets push <slug> --dotenv .env` (makefun secrets push, from inside the unpacked kit), which reads the NAME=value lines from the file (--stdin in place of --dotenv: from standard input), never a value from its arguments, or PUT /api/competitions/<slug>/secrets with {"secrets": {"NAME": "value"}} and your API key as x-api-key. list_secrets lists them; remove_secret, `node cli/makefun.mjs secrets rm <slug> <NAME>` or DELETE /api/competitions/<slug>/secrets/<NAME> removes one (pushing a new value replaces it): no run gets it from then on, and its sealed copy is erased at once, unless a final-phase run of yours ran with it: then make.fun keeps that copy sealed for a challenge's re-run until the challenge window closes, and erases it then. Every value is erased once the competition's challenge window ends.

phase.description: dev (the default) or final (once the final phase is finalized: get_competition's phases say when)

slug.description: The competition slug, e.g. chess-engine-01 (list_competitions lists them)

name: get_kit

build_key.description: Your own build key on a metered competition (its state, never its secret); absent signed out and where the competition has no build allowance

secrets.description: Your own entry secrets in a competition whose entries make.fun runs (names, lanes, hints and check states, never a value); absent signed out, where the competition runs no entry code, and where you hold none and no push is taken

title: Get a bounty's kit
